thread:
Nate (Zenith-pay): Hey team — since last night we've been seeing a lot of 429s from the API, ~20% p95 for a subset of keys. Happens in bursts around :00 and :15. Logging shows `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0` most of the time. Can someone help triage?

Aisha (Support): Sorry you're hitting that, Nate. Can you paste one of the request IDs and a short sample of headers from one failed request? Also which region and model endpoint?

Nate (Zenith-pay): Request-ID: rc_9f2b3c. Region: us-west-2. Endpoint: /v1/generate (r-render). Headers from failed attempt: ```
X-RateLimit-Limit: 3600/hour; 60/min
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 2024-03-15T00:01:12Z
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
```

deploy-bot: automatic alert — spike detected for api-key zpay-prod in us-west-2 (15:03 UTC). Aggregate RPM jumped 6x for 90s.

Tom (SRE): thanks. Can you confirm whether these requests are long-lived streams or short synchronous calls? Also, are you multiplexing many users on a single API key?

Nate (Zenith-pay): short calls, mostly 600-900ms each. We do pool connections and run up to 60 concurrent workers per process; have 5 processes per pod. So ~300 concurrent. We've been batching user requests client-side for throughput.

Aisha (Support): that concurrency math explains it — per-key rate limits are per token bucket. If you multiply workers x pods you can spike into the per-minute cap even if average RPM looks fine. In your case 300 concurrent * ~1 req / sec ~= 18k RPM burst potential.

Maya (Eng): quick check — I pulled the metric for zpay-prod from the last 3 hours. Confirmed sharp spikes at minute boundaries: see `requests_per_minute` graph (us-west-2) with peaks hitting the per-minute cap. The token bucket refill happens once per minute, so aligned cron-like traffic or synchronized retries will fold into spike windows.

Tom (SRE): repro steps you can try locally to emulate the fold: ```bash
# 300 concurrent short requests, 1s per request
seq 1 300 | xargs -n1 -P300 -I{} curl -s -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
That will often produce many 429s even if averaged RPM < account limit.

Maya (Eng): Also share a snippet of your retry/backoff config — naive fixed-interval retries without jitter will re-sync and worsen folding.

Nate (Zenith-pay): our retry is naive: `for i in range(3): sleep(1); retry()` — yep, no jitter.

Aisha (Support): ok short-term options: 1) reduce client concurrency to safe levels (we recommend <= 25 concurrent connections per API key for this workload), 2) add exponential backoff + full jitter, 3) stagger cron/worker start times, 4) request a rate limit increase if you legitimately need sustained concurrency (we can escalate).

Maya (Eng): long-term/server-side mitigations we can offer: prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts, or move heavy traffic to a Dedicated pool where you get reserved capacity and per-second smoothing. We can also enable soft-smoothing at the edge (reduce minute-bucket folding) but that's an ops change and requires approval.

Tom (SRE): quick patch I'd try: cap concurrency per process to 16 and add jittered backoff. Example python backoff: ```python
import random, time
def backoff(attempt):
    delay = (2 ** attempt) * 0.1
    time.sleep(delay * random.random())
```
That usually evens out retries across window.

Nate (Zenith-pay): doing that now — will roll a canary to one pod with concurrency=16 and retry jitter. Will report back in 15 min.

Aisha (Support): while you roll, can you also attach one failing request log (full headers + request_id) to the ticket so we can tie it in? I'll hold an escalation if the canary doesn't fully resolve it.

deploy-bot: incident status changed — investigating -> monitoring.

Tom (SRE): fyi, if you need a temporary quota bump we can open an emergency request: what sustained TPS do you need? (provide 95th pct sustained, not just burst).

Nate (Zenith-pay): sustained target would be ~900 RPS peak (non-bursty) for a 10-min window. Right now that's impossible with our single key.

Maya (Eng): note — 900 RPS sustained across one API key is large (would need Dedicated or multi-key sharding). Suggest two paths: A) shard traffic across multiple API keys and token-bucket evenly, B) apply for Dedicated plan. For B I'll prepare an ops note to speed approval.

Aisha (Support): next steps agreed: - Nate rolls canary with concurrency cap + jitter (in-flight) - Nate attach failing request logs to ticket - If canary fails, Aisha to request temporary quota increase while Maya opens Dedicated evaluation.

Nate (Zenith-pay): Canary rolled. Initial numbers: 429s dropped from ~18% -> ~2% in the canary pod. Rolling to remaining pods now. Thanks! :thumbsup:

Aisha (Support): great — keep us posted. I'll convert this thread into a short runbook entry for similar customer patterns and link here.

Maya (Eng): adding noted mitigations to internal docs: client jitter, concurrency guidance, and Dedicated upgrade path.

Nate (Zenith-pay): attaching the sample request log now (rc_9f2b3c). I'll follow up if anything pops back up.

Tom (SRE): marking this as resolved-in-flight; reopen if 429 > 5% after full rollout.

Aisha (Support): resolved-in-canary -> monitoring. Will close after 24h stable. :white_check_mark:
